To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mutation of the PBj-Nefa diacidic motif impairs T-cell proliferation and enteropathic disease in pig-tail macaques.
(1) mutation of a diacid motif in Nef of the SIV-PB virus abolishes the enteropathic disease and (2) this effect is due to the impairment of Nef-mediated signaling in T cells.
mutation of the PBj-Nefa diacidic motif abolishes disease progression and T-cell activation in pig-tailed monkeys despite efficient virus replication.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pathogenic mechanisms of SIV-PBjo and SIV-PBjm.
the molecular mechanisms of SIV-induced immune activation.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms that are involved in the pathogenesis of lentiviral infections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the diacidic domain in SIVsmm-PBj-Nef is required for T cell activation in vivo.

the diacidic motifs in the Nef proteins of pathogenic SIVs and HIV-1 may be important for the activation of the ERK1/2 MAPK pathway, leading to T-cell proliferation, and thus may be involved in the pathogenicity of the virus.
the diacidic Nef motif is a key factor in SIV-Pbj pathogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mutation of the Nef diacidic motif of SIV-PBjo virus abolishes disease progression despite efficient replication in vivo.
a mutation of a diacid motif in SIV PBj Nef protein impairs T-cell proliferation and enteropathic disease.
the diacidic motifs in Nef are essential for the pathogenicity of the SIV-PBjo virus and the Nef protein is a key player for the pathogenic course of the SIV infection in macaques.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a mutation of a single motif within the Nef protein can alter the pathogenesis of a virus, and that the diacidic motifs in Nef proteins of nonpathogenic SIV strains may contribute to the nonpathogenic phenotype of these strains.
Nef proteins of pathogenic lentiviruses are able to induce T-cell activation and proliferation and that this activity is a major determinant of pathogenesis.
the diacidic Nef motif of the PBj Nef protein is critical for T-cell activation in vivo.
